# Test fixtures

## Provenance, honestly

`filing_history.json` and `document_metadata.json` are **hand-written to the
shape documented for the Companies House API. They are not recorded responses**
— nobody has run this against the live service yet. They are correct as far as
the published field names go, and they are enough to drive every branch in
`docintel/ingest/corpus.py`, but they cannot prove that the live API agrees.

The first real run with an API key is the moment to replace these with genuine
recordings. Until then, treat any test that passes here as evidence about our
code and not about Companies House.

The company number `00445790` appears in them as a plausible-looking value. The
tests do not depend on it being any particular real company.

## The PDFs

`text_layer.pdf` and `scanned.pdf` are generated by `make_pdfs.py`, which is
committed next to them so the bytes are auditable rather than magic. Run it and
the files should come back byte-identical.

- `text_layer.pdf` — three pages of real text operators, with deliberately
  unequal amounts of text (38, 60 and 353 extracted characters) so that the
  median (60) and the mean (150) differ. A fixture with equal pages would pass
  whether `analyse_pdf` computed the median or the mean.
- `scanned.pdf` — one page whose only content is an image XObject, no text
  operator anywhere. pypdf opens it happily and extracts nothing, which is the
  shape of a scanned filing.

Both parse without emitting a warning, which matters because the suite runs
with `filterwarnings = ["error"]`.
